Northern Colorado's market is shifting — and it's buyer-friendly. 🏡

With more inventory and steady rates, sellers are offering concessions again: covering closing costs, rate buydowns, and more.

Our new Buyer Concession Cheat Sheet breaks down exactly how much sellers can contribute by loan type (conventional, FHA, VA), how to ask for closing-cost help, and how to stack concessions with CHFA down payment assistance in Fort Collins, Loveland, Windsor, and Greeley.

Learn more at the link below.

🤝 Buyer concessions are back in Northern Colorado — here's what that means for you.

Our August market update flagged it: with more inventory and steady rates, sellers are increasingly offering concessions to get deals done — covering closing costs, rate buydowns, even prepaids. That's the most buyer-friendly conditions we've seen since 2022.

New on the blog: the Buyer Concession Cheat Sheet. It breaks down:
• Maximum seller contributions by loan type — conventional, FHA, VA (yes, the limits differ)
• How to ask for closing-cost assistance the right way
• How to stack concessions with CHFA down payment assistance in Fort Collins, Loveland, Windsor & Greeley
• What counts as a legitimate concession vs. a red flag

We also refreshed the market data on our Loveland, Fort Collins, Greeley, and Windsor city pages — median prices, inventory, and days on market, updated for mid-2026.

Whether you're a first-time buyer using CHFA or a move-up buyer in the $500K–$650K range, this guide shows you exactly what leverage you have at the negotiating table.

Read the full guide → https://saahomes.com/blog/buyer-concession-cheat-sheet-northern-colorado/

Adam & Mandi Schwartz | SAA Homes
